subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This chooses a scheduled-run security boundary and public config/default contract, including whether existing cron jobs that directly use `message` during announce delivery keep working by default.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and upgrade-safe tests for message-tool denial across cron delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface while coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Leave cron restrictions to `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery mitigations, accepting the current operator ergonomics and defense-in-depth gap.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and upgrade-safe tests for message-tool denial across cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from scoped conversation capability work, current tool-policy pipeline ownership, and prior review context for this issue.
